mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and increases S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns do not show a positive trend when FEDFUNDS is low, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive when UNRATE exceeds 5%, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand, boosting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns do not increase with rising HOUST, the hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: Growing industrial production signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns do not correlate with INDPRO growth, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in retail sales and housing starts indicates strong demand, boosting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns do not increase when both RSAFS and HOUST grow, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate and falling unemployment indicate tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive under these conditions, the hypothesis fails.
